subject: food-technology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: How many food groups are shown on the Eatwell Guide?
questions.explain: The Eatwell Guide divides foods into five groups to show the proportions of a healthy, balanced diet.

questions.q: According to the '5 A DAY' message, how many portions of fruit and vegetables should be eaten each day?
questions.explain: The '5 A DAY' guidance recommends eating at least five portions of a variety of fruit and vegetables daily.

questions.q: Taking folic acid before and during early pregnancy helps to prevent which condition in the developing baby?
options: Neural tube defects such as spina bifida
questions.explain: Folic acid supports the correct development of the baby's spine, reducing the risk of neural tube defects such as spina bifida.

questions.q: A person with coeliac disease must follow a diet that avoids gluten, which is found in:
questions.explain: Gluten is a protein found in wheat, barley and rye, so people with coeliac disease must avoid these grains.

questions.q: What is the main function of calcium in the diet?
questions.explain: Calcium is essential for building and maintaining strong bones and teeth.

questions.q: A shortage of iron in the diet is most likely to lead to:
questions.explain: Iron is needed to make haemoglobin, so a lack of iron can cause iron-deficiency anaemia.

questions.q: Besides oily fish, what is the main natural source of vitamin D?
options: The action of sunlight on the skin
questions.explain: Vitamin D is made in the skin through the action of sunlight, as well as being found in oily fish and fortified foods.

questions.q: Which foods does a vegan diet exclude?
questions.explain: A vegan diet excludes all foods of animal origin, including meat, fish, eggs, dairy and honey.

questions.q: Why do adolescent girls have a particularly high requirement for iron?
options: To replace iron lost during menstruation
Because they grow taller than boys
questions.explain: Blood is lost during menstruation, so adolescent girls need extra iron to replace it and avoid anaemia.

questions.q: Older adults are encouraged to have enough calcium and vitamin D mainly to reduce the risk of:
questions.explain: Adequate calcium and vitamin D help maintain bone density and lower the risk of osteoporosis in later life.

questions.q: Including a source of vitamin C in a meal is helpful because it:
options: Improves absorption of iron from plant foods
Produces vitamin D in the body
questions.explain: Vitamin C increases the absorption of non-haem (plant) iron, which is useful in vegetarian and vegan diets.

questions.q: Why must vegans take particular care to obtain enough vitamin B12?
options: It is found mainly in animal foods
It is destroyed by cooking vegetables
It is only made in sunlight
It is found only in vegetable oils
questions.explain: Vitamin B12 occurs naturally in animal foods, so vegans need fortified foods or supplements to avoid deficiency.

questions.q: Why is folic acid especially important around conception and in the first 12 weeks of pregnancy?
options: The baby's spine and nervous system develop very early
The mother gains most weight then
The baby's teeth form during this time
questions.explain: The neural tube forms in the earliest weeks, so folic acid is needed before many women even realise they are pregnant.

questions.q: Weaning, the introduction of solid foods to a baby, is usually recommended to begin from around:
questions.explain: Solid foods are generally introduced from around six months, when milk alone no longer meets the baby's needs.

questions.q: Vitamin D is important in the diet partly because it helps the body to:
questions.explain: Vitamin D is needed for the absorption of calcium, which is why the two nutrients work together for healthy bones.

questions.q: A person managing type 2 diabetes should pay particular attention to:
options: Controlling their intake of free sugars
questions.explain: Limiting free sugars helps to control blood glucose levels, which is central to managing diabetes.

questions.q: When planning a main meal for a guest who has coeliac disease, the best choice would be:
options: Grilled chicken with rice and vegetables
Pasta bake made with wheat pasta
Steak pie with a pastry crust
questions.explain: Rice is naturally gluten-free, whereas breadcrumbs, wheat pasta and pastry all contain gluten.

questions.q: Which dish would best help boost folic acid intake for a pregnant woman?
options: A leafy green vegetable and fortified cereal dish
questions.explain: Leafy green vegetables and fortified breakfast cereals are good sources of folate and folic acid.

questions.q: An elderly person with a small appetite needs to meet their nutritional needs. The best approach is to:
options: Offer small, nutrient-dense meals and snacks
Serve one very large meal each day
questions.explain: Small, frequent nutrient-dense meals help ensure enough nutrients are eaten despite a reduced appetite.

questions.q: Following the proportions of the Eatwell Guide, the largest part of the diet should come from:
options: Foods high in fat and sugar
questions.explain: The Eatwell Guide shows fruit and vegetables and starchy carbohydrates as the two largest groups, forming the basis of the diet.
